html:
On 1 September 1920 the French general Henri Gouraud proclaimed the State of Greater Lebanon in Beirut, under the French mandate that followed the fall of the Ottoman Empire.

Maronite leaders had asked France for a larger Lebanon that could stand on its own. To Mount Lebanon were added the coastal cities of Beirut, Tripoli, Sidon and Tyre and the Bekaa valley. The new state was far more mixed: Sunni and Shia Muslims made up close to half the people, and many of them wanted to be part of Syria.

It became the Lebanese Republic in 1926 and independent in 1943, with power shared between religions by the National Pact. That balance, and its breakdown, shaped the civil war of 1975. See also the French mandate.
sum: On 1 September 1920 the French general Henri Gouraud proclaimed the State of Greater Lebanon in Beirut, under the French mandate that followed the fall of the Ottoman Empire.
